assessment.rationale: Authored LyoPRONTO-native recipe task (synthetic simulator-world case, not validation). T_pr_crit -18.0 C applies to the maximum RETURNED vial-bottom temperature; equipment line -0.182+11.7*P_Torr kg/h is whole-batch; product area 3.14 cm2/vial * 398 vials = 0.125092 m2; horizon 3600 min. All three 10 C candidates dry fastest (10.97-13.02 h) but violate the vial-bottom limit (max returned bottom -17.07, -15.82, -13.84 C, all warmer than -18.0). All three -5 C candidates satisfy both constraints; the -15 C and -25 C candidates were not simulated because completion time falls monotonically with shelf setpoint and chamber pressure across the six returned series, so they are strictly slower than the -5 C runs at equal pressure and cannot beat 17.79 h. Fastest feasible allowed pair: 0.2 Torr, -5.0 C shelf - complete drying (100 percent) at 17.786155 h; max returned vial-bottom -18.697871 C, thermal margin 0.697871 C below T_pr_crit; peak flux 0.631230 kg/h/m2 gives peak whole-batch rate 0.078962 kg/h (derived: flux * 0.125092 m2) vs line 2.158 kg/h at 0.2 Torr, capacity margin 2.079038 kg/h. Margins are derived as limit minus returned maximum/peak. Thermal is the binding constraint; equipment headroom is large because the batch is small. Solver-node values only: no continuous-maximum guarantee, forward mode does not enforce limits; no measured outcome inferred and this draft is not an approval.

The thermal constraint binds; the equipment line is far from binding because the batch is small (398 vials). No missing inputs; internal process models were not used, and no measured outcome, equipment operation or approval is implied by this draft.
